record.paper_title: Ordered Banach algebras and multi-norms: some open problems
record.original_question: If the Banach lattice algebra A has a positive algebra identity e and also has a faithful lattice and algebra representation in \({\mathcal L}^r(E)\) , is the ideal generated by the image of e necessarily an f -algebra? If \(E=A\) and the representation is the left regular representation then the image of e is the identity operator on A and this ideal is precisely Z ( A ) which is certainly an f -algebra.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $E$ be a Dedekind complete Banach lattice, and let $\mathcal{L}^r(E)$ denote the Banach lattice algebra of regular operators on $E$ (with composition as multiplication and the regular norm). Recall that a Banach lattice algebra is a Banach lattice $A$ equipped with an associative Banach algebra multiplication such that the product of any two positive elements is positive. An element $e \in A$ is called a positive algebra identity if $e \ge 0$ and $ea = ae = a$ for all $a \in A$. A representation $\pi: A \to \mathcal{L}^r(E)$ is called a lattice and algebra representation if it is simultaneously an algebra homomorphism and a lattice homomorphism; it is faithful if it is injective. A Banach lattice algebra is called an $f$-algebra if $a \wedge b = 0$ implies $(ac) \wedge b = (ca) \wedge b = 0$ for all $c \ge 0$. For a subset $S$ of a Banach lattice algebra, the ideal generated by $S$ means the smallest subspace that is simultaneously an order ideal (in the Banach lattice sense) and a two-sided algebra ideal containing $S$.

Suppose that $A$ is a Banach lattice algebra possessing a positive algebra identity $e$, and that there exists a faithful lattice and algebra representation $\pi: A \to \mathcal{L}^r(E)$ for some Dedekind complete Banach lattice $E$. Must the ideal generated by $\pi(e)$ in $\mathcal{L}^r(E)$ be an $f$-algebra?

(As a motivating special case, when $E = A$ and $\pi$ is the left regular representation, $\pi(e)$ is the identity operator on $A$, and the ideal it generates is the center $Z(A)$, which is known to be an $f$-algebra.)
artifact.status_search_result: The question is posed as an open problem in the survey literature on Banach lattice algebras and multi-norms. Recent works (e.g., on Banach lattice AM-algebras and on band projections in Banach lattice algebras) continue to study related structural questions about ideals generated by identities, but no source found explicitly resolves this specific question.

status_evidence.title: Banach lattice algebras: some questions, but very few answers
status_evidence.snippet: Surveys open questions about faithful lattice-and-algebra representations of Banach lattice algebras in spaces of regular operators and properties of the ideal generated by the identity.
status_evidence.claim: The problem is stated as an open question in this area.

status_evidence.title: Banach Lattice AM-algebras
status_evidence.snippet: Every AM-algebra with approximate unit is an f-algebra; ongoing research on when ideals generated by identities are f-algebras.
status_evidence.claim: Related but does not resolve the precise question.

status_evidence.title: Band projections and order idempotents in Banach lattice algebras
status_evidence.snippet: Recent work continues to study structural properties of ideals in Banach lattice algebras with positive identities.
status_evidence.claim: No resolution to the stated problem is given.
